title: An omitted component interaction biases never-administered regimens and leaks into regimens that do not contain it
question: When additivity makes a never-administered combination estimable, how far can an omitted component interaction move its predicted effect, and does it contaminate other regimens?
design: Exact calculation on an eight-trial component network with three co-administered and three never co-administered component pairs; synergy of three magnitudes placed on one pair, both kinds, or all pairs; additive and prespecified-interaction models.
answer: No. At a synergy of 0.2 (twice a contrast's SE), 15 of 32 never-administered regimen results that the additive model reported as estimable had 95% coverage below 0.90, down to 0.11. Synergy on a never co-administered pair went wholly into the regimens containing it and was undetectable; synergy on a co-administered pair was absorbed into the component effects and biased regimens without that pair by -0.125, including a never-administered one. Modeling co-administered pairs' interactions removed the leakage. The share of a regimen's pairs never co-administered did not flag the failures (AUROC 0.37).
findings: Synergy on C+D (never co-administered): regimens containing C+D biased by 0.2, coverage 0.63 to 0.71; all others exact.
Synergy on A+B (co-administered): B+C and B+D biased by -0.125 (coverage 0.73 and 0.81) though neither contains A+B.
Interaction model for the co-administered pairs: unbiased when the synergy is on a co-administered pair, no help for C+D.
not_answered: One connected network, continuous outcome, fixed effect; no disconnection, covariate adjustment, selection procedures or formal synergy bound. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Effect of each two- to four-component regimen against placebo
methods_compared: component model with interactions for co-administered pairs
n_sim: Exact calculation: 4 synergy locations x 3 magnitudes x 2 models x 11 regimens
